9: "And yeish omrim, specifically gezeilos, etc." — The Sma wrote that the Mechaber holds we judge all gezeilos except gezeilos that come by way of chavalos, following the view of the Tosafos in Perek HaChovel (Bava Kama 84) and the beginning of the first perek of Sanhedrin. (And it is in this way that the Mishnah at the beginning of perek 1 of Sanhedrin is dealing, and so it is proven in Tosafos there — and not like the Maharsha at the beginning of perek 1 of Sanhedrin, see there.) And therefore the Mechaber wrote without qualification that we judge all gezeilos. End of his words. And this is difficult to me: if so, the Mechaber should have written "gezeilos that come by way of chavalos." And there is a further difficulty: he didn't bring the words of the Tosafos on this in the Beis Yosef. Therefore it appears to me that the Mechaber holds like the view of the Rambam, who wrote without qualification that we judge all gezeilos. And what we say in Gittin Perek HaMegaresh (daf 88 amud beis), that gezeilos and chavalos we do not judge because they are not shechiach — this refers to the kenas of gezeilos, such as tashlumei kefel and daled v'hei and similar, which are lo shechiach. And indeed [the Gemara] could have said that they don't have chisaron kis, but it only said it this way [referring to lack of shechiach] on account of the chavalos. And so it is precise in the language of the Rambam in perek 5 of Hilchos Sanhedrin, where he wrote: "Dinei kenasos, such as gezeilos and chavalos and tashlumei kefel, etc. — we do not judge, etc. One who stole or robbed — we collect from him the keren [via] dayanei chutz la'aretz, but the tosefes (the addition) we do not collect, etc." And with this is removed the difficulty of the Maharshal in Perek HaChovel siman 5, who wrote: "It's astonishing that the Rambam wrote that gezeilos and chavalos we don't judge in chutz la'aretz, and afterwards wrote 'one who stole or robbed, etc.'" And so it appears to me to be the view of the Rosh at the beginning of perek 1 of Sanhedrin and the Tur, who wrote without qualification that all gezeilos are shechiach and we judge them. And so it appears to me to be the view of Rav Hai, whom the Tur brings later at the end of siman 420 — and not like the Maharshal there who wrote that in their view gezeilos that come by way of chavalos we do not judge. And therefore the Mechaber wrote here without qualification: "One who stole or robbed — we collect from him the keren." This is based on what he brought in his Beis Yosef in the words of the Rambam, and it is implied in his Beis Yosef that the view of the Rosh and the Tur is also so. And see in the Tur and Beis Yosef later at the beginning of siman 30. And so it appears to be the main view for halacha, as the Tosafos and other later authorities wrote, that it is a daily practice (ma'asim b'chol yom) to judge dinei gezeilos, see there. (And the words of the Bach in the view of the Rosh are mixed up. At the beginning he wrote that Rabbeinu Yerucham, according to his view, wrote like the Tosafos that gezeilos coming by way of chavalos we don't judge. And at the end he wrote that the view of the Rosh is like the Rambam. And in truth, one who examines Rabbeinu Yerucham will see that he didn't write this way except in the name of the Tosafos of the Rosh, see there.)
